description: Sou um apreciador da forma como jogos digitais podem ser implementados para ensino e entretenimento. Proponho levar conhecimentos técnicos e científicos para todos os públicos de forma lúdica e divertida, dessa forma, instigando a busca e participação na ciência.
summary:
18 Days in Space is a browser-based educational game for children aged 7 to 12, built with Godot Engine 4 for the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge. Players become the Commander of a lunar outpost that has lost contact with Earth and must keep the crew alive for 18 days until a rescue ship arrives.

Each day, players distribute limited solar energy among life support (oxygen and food), radiation shielding, and optional scientific research, while random events such as meteors, equipment failures, and solar storms force quick decisions. These trade-offs mirror the competing demands the challenge describes. The game is grounded in real NASA data: ISS ECLSS-inspired life support, DONKI space weather data for solar storms, and public-domain NASA images unlocked in a gallery, alongside a glossary of technical terms. It is available in English and Portuguese.

It matters because it turns complex mission-planning concepts into hands-on, memorable experiences, inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details:
18 Days in Space is a browser-based serious game for children aged 7 to 12. Players are the Commander of a lunar outpost that has lost contact with Earth, and they must keep the crew alive for 18 days until a rescue ship arrives. Each day, they distribute limited solar energy among life support, radiation shielding, and optional research, while random events like meteors, equipment failures, and solar storms force quick decisions. Research unlocks real NASA images in a gallery, with a glossary explaining technical terms.

The game lets children experience the trade-offs behind real mission planning by making decisions and seeing the consequences, which we hope will spark curiosity about space science and engineering. It is free, needs no installation, and is available in English and Portuguese, so it can be used in classrooms and at home.

We built it with Godot Engine 4 and GDScript, exported to HTML5, with progress saved via IndexedDB and a UI based on the NEONIX asset pack. The architecture follows SOLID principles, with custom Resources and signals, so designers can add new events without touching the code.

The project is creative in turning a complex scenario into a simple, tense daily puzzle. An event "pity system" keeps the pressure rising, and unlocking real NASA imagery keeps players motivated. We also grounded it in real data, including ISS life support systems, DONKI space weather data, and "Fast Transit" trajectories to the Lunar Gateway, simplified for a young audience. All gallery images are public domain.
